unmapped_findings: For the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni (Fe–28Mn–9Al-0.9C) alloy in HR+CR+1023 K, the cold rolled microstructure transformed from partial recrystallization at 973 K to complete recrystallization at 1023 K; the fraction of recrystallized austenite at ~1023 K (intermediate data point) lies between 0.8 and 1.0 (Fig. 5a).

A 50 K increase in heat treatment temperature (973 K → 1023 K) for 28Mn0Ni accelerated the recrystallization kinetics but caused a drastic reduction in strength (from YS ~900 MPa / 23% elongation at 973 K to YS 732 MPa / 36% elongation at 1023 K) (b0079).

No Vickers hardness data point is reported explicitly for 28Mn0Ni at 1023 K; Fig. 8b plots hardness against heat treatment temperature at 873, 973, 1073, 1173 and 1273 K only. For 28Mn0Ni hardness decreases monotonically with heat treatment temperature.

XRD patterns (Fig. 2a) for 28Mn0Ni were reported only for HR+CR, HR+CR+973 K and HR+CR+1173 K conditions; no XRD trace at 1023 K is given. At 973 K additional peaks of κ-carbide and B2 appear, whereas at 1173 K only γ peaks remain.

TEM analysis for 28Mn0Ni was reported at 973 K (mixed recrystallized/deformed austenite with intragranular κ-carbides 10–60 nm and intergranular B2) and at 1173 K (precipitate-free); no TEM data specific to the 1023 K condition is provided.

In tensile tests the 28Mn0Ni alloy in HR+CR+1023 K exhibited significant ductility (36 ± 2 %) in contrast to the 15Mn5Ni alloy which was brittle (<1%) under the same condition; post-tensile fractography specific to 28Mn0Ni was reported for the 1023 K condition showing ductile dimple rupture.
